dramatic.state_in: Localized alteration is possible; stopping separately from draw remains unresolved.
dramatic.state_out: Greg can alter what the response is doing after STOP but cannot hold it unchanged.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns stop/release distinction; Greg owns moment-to-moment report.

performance.pressure: The hard part is control after initiation.
performance.behavior: Greg notices widening and reports it before it becomes larger; Hessa refuses both catastrophic and triumphant interpretation.

screenplay: Two forearm marks create a choice after draw.
Greg shapes toward the called mark.
Hessa says STOP while keeping draw.
Forward motion reduces, but the patch broadens sideways.
Greg reports spreading; Hessa orders release.
They name exactly what did and did not stop.

dramatic.state_in: Greg is ready to train but still carries old support assumptions into turns.
dramatic.required_result: Stress turning and route choice with changing geometry rather than teach a fixed technique.
dramatic.state_out: Greg identifies exposed-side problems and learns to choose before moving away from obstruction.
dramatic.ownership: Pessa owns task geometry; Greg owns movement choices/report.

performance.pressure: Pessa keeps removing a tidy rule.
performance.behavior: She changes stake positions and body placement; Greg learns every configuration trades one problem for another.
performance.relationship: Pessa respects him by refusing to simplify his body for him.

screenplay: Pessa plants irregular stakes and calls destinations unpredictably.
She steps into expected crutch placement, forcing Greg to stop.
With one crutch he feels spatially exposed and reacts too sharply to blocked space.
He recovers a small hop without being caught.
They rest, then test a fallen stake as route obstruction.
Greg chooses around it before later trying to cross it, keeping choice central.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: each stop is movement state

dramatic.required_result: Test whether ending deliberate feed lets alteration settle toward underlying draw.
dramatic.state_out: Alteration diminishes, followed by a tiny wrist twitch.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns framing/stop conditions; Greg owns subjective process.

performance.pressure: A wording change must create a truly different task.
performance.behavior: Hessa introduces ENOUGH; Greg follows it more cleanly and promptly reports the twitch.
performance.relationship: They design around Greg's literalism instead of fighting it.

screenplay: A draw-only check proves yesterday's crutch load did not produce symptoms.
Hessa reframes STOP as ENOUGH: stop feeding, do not freeze.
Greg shapes a narrow forearm alteration.
On ENOUGH it softens while draw remains.
A tiny wrist twitch appears; Hessa orders release.
They call it closer to instruction, not success.

dramatic.state_in: Greg is adapting physically and expanding socially into theatre with Lyssa.
dramatic.required_result: Turn a comedy date into an evacuation revealing accessibility constraints and theatre competence.
dramatic.state_out: Greg exits through backstage and discovers the working machine behind performance.
dramatic.ownership: Lyssa owns decision to leave; ushers own routing; Greg owns which routes he can physically manage.

performance.pressure: Pivot from delight to danger without making Greg helpless.
performance.behavior: Lyssa checks but keeps moving when crowd geometry separates them; Greg rejects unrailed steps and is rerouted level backstage.
performance.relationship: Lyssa trusts his self-report; Greg lets her move.

screenplay: Greg gradually forgets the exits because the comedy is genuinely funny.
Smoke appears; actors continue while ushers start a controlled clear-out.
Crowd flow separates Greg and Lyssa; he signals her to keep moving.
An usher offers three unrailed steps; Greg asks useful questions and refuses.
He is redirected backstage because it is level.
A painted tree nearly hits him as he enters the machinery behind the show.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: action fragmentation is pressure/route geometry

dramatic.state_in: Greg is stable after evacuation and wants the next magic question.
dramatic.required_result: Test deliberate reduction rather than passive settling.
dramatic.state_out: Greg partially reduces but introduces elbowward shift and finger-curl urge.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns safety/interpretation; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants the clean next rung.
performance.behavior: Hessa frames RETURN as active reduction; Greg stops when movement changes unexpectedly and reports motor urge before actual movement.

screenplay: Hessa first tests distraction during minimal draw.
She marks the forearm and introduces deliberate RETURN.
Greg shapes, pauses at ENOUGH, then tries to reduce while keeping draw.
The patch shifts toward the elbow.
On a smaller correction it narrows, but fingers want to curl.
Hessa orders immediate release and records both reduction and warning sign.
